body.statement: Using \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{adapt}}\), determine the smallest deterministic penalty sequence \(\ell_n\ge1\) for which a fully data-driven estimator and confidence interval, not given \(\kappa\), \(c_-\), \(c_+\), \(r_{0n}\), \(r_{1n}\), or \(r_{en}\), attain uniform risk and honest expected length at most \(C\ell_n\rho_n\) over compact ranges of these indices; prove a matching adaptation lower bound for \(\ell_n\).
body.justification: The oracle theorem exposes but does not resolve the practical cost of learning which of the four obstructions is active.
body.gap: MaWang2020RobustIPW has data-driven trimming for an IPW asymptotic criterion, while the supplied theorem assumes known shell and nuisance certificates; no exact adaptation penalty is available.
body.consumer: The answer determines whether the oracle clipping and interval benchmarks can be implemented from validation data without an avoidable logarithmic loss.

obligation.what_is_open: The smallest adaptation penalty and its matching lower bound when the tail exponent, both shell constants, and all three nuisance radii are unknown.
obligation.obstruction: The proved oracle threshold uses the unknown quantities in three competing scales. The frozen adaptation handle does not specify observable confidence bounds for the global approximation errors, and the fixed certificates used in the oracle proof cannot be recovered uniformly from a validation sample without additional structure on the public predictors. Honest interval adaptation also requires a between-class testing argument not supplied by the fixed-index lower families.
obligation.attempted: A dyadic Lepski comparison controls stochastic differences between clipped scores, but its deterministic clipping biases contain \(r_{1n}\lambda^{\kappa/2}\), \(r_{1n}r_{en}/\lambda\), and \(r_{0n}r_{en}\), none of which has a uniformly estimable upper certificate under the frozen model. Reusing empirical shell counts estimates the observed propensity tail only after controlling the unknown propensity approximation error, which is the same unidentified radius entering the choice.
obligation.partial_result: With \(\kappa\), \(c_-\), \(c_+\), and the certified radii supplied, thm:clipped-absolute-upper, lem:median-risk-upgrade, and thm:honest-interval-frontier attain risk and expected length of order \(\rho_n\), so the oracle adaptation penalty is \(1\). No claim about the unknown-index penalty follows from the frozen primitives.
